definition: Fugitive concealment; secret retirement; hiding.
sense: Fugitive concealment; secret retirement; hiding. [R.] Phillips.

definition: Evil or corrupt usage; abuse; wrong; reproach; deception; cheat.
sense: Evil or corrupt usage; abuse; wrong; reproach; deception; cheat. Chaucer.
etym: OE. abusion, abusioun, OF. abusion, fr. L. abusio misuse of words, f. abuti. See Abuse, v. t.

definition: The act of burning, or heating to dryness; the state of being thus heated or dried.
sense: The act of burning, or heating to dryness; the state of being thus heated or dried. [Obs.] Harvey.
etym: L. adustio, fr. adurere, adustum: cf. F. adustion.

definition: Executed in a workmanlike manner; ingeniously made.
sense: Executed in a workmanlike manner; ingeniously made. [R.]
author: Bailey

definition: A pole set up as the sign of an alehouse.
sense: A pole set up as the sign of an alehouse. [Obs.]

definition: Divination by means of flour.
sense: Divination by means of flour. Encyc. Brit.

definition: As if dead; lifeless; spiritless; dejected; depressed.
sense: As if dead; lifeless; spiritless; dejected; depressed. Shak.
etym: Pref. a- + F. mort death, dead; all amort is for alamort.

definition: Mystical; having a secondary spiritual meaning.
sense: Mystical; having a secondary spiritual meaning; as, the rest of the Sabbath, in an anagogical sense, signifies the repose of the saints in heaven; an anagogical explication. -- An`a*gog"ic*al*ly, adv.

definition: Pertaining to mind or spirit; spiritual.
sense: Pertaining to mind or spirit; spiritual.

definition: Snatched away; seized or possessed, as a demoniac; raving; mad; crack-brained.
sense: Snatched away; seized or possessed, as a demoniac; raving; mad; crack-brained. [Obs.]
author: Howell

definition: Without a material body; incorporeal.
sense: Without a material body; incorporeal. Todd.

definition: Wanting reverence; void of respectful fear.
sense: Wanting reverence; void of respectful fear. "Awless insolence." Dryden.

definition: A signal fire; an alarm fire.
sense: A signal fire; an alarm fire.
quote: Sweet Teviot! on thy silver tide The glaring balefires blaze no more.
author: Sir W. Scott
etym: AS. b the fire of the b fire, flame (akin to Icel. bal, OSlav. b, white, Gr. bright, white, Skr. bhala brightness) + f, E. fire.

definition: To make swollen and disfigured or sullied by weeping.
sense: To make swollen and disfigured or sullied by weeping; as, her eyes or cheeks were beblubbered.

definition: To involve in darkness; to shroud with the shades of night; to obscure.
sense: To involve in darkness; to shroud with the shades of night; to obscure. [Archaic]
author: Garth

definition: Out of one's senses; distracted; mad.
sense: Out of one's senses; distracted; mad. [Obs.] Shak.
etym: Pref. be- + straught; prob. here used for distraught.

definition: To weep over; to deplore; to bedew with tears.
sense: To weep over; to deplore; to bedew with tears. "His timeless death beweeping." Drayton.

definition: One who hides away books, as in a tomb.
sense: One who hides away books, as in a tomb. [R.] Crabb.

definition: The night in which a person is born; the anniversary of that night in succeeding years.
sense: The night in which a person is born; the anniversary of that night in succeeding years.
quote: The angelic song in Bethlehem field, On thy birthnight, that sung thee Savior born.
author: Milton

definition: A liquor made of ale and honey fermented, with spices, etc.
sense: A liquor made of ale and honey fermented, with spices, etc. [Obs.] B. Jonson.
etym: OE. braket, bragot, fr. W. bragawd, bragod, fr. brag malt.

definition: A stake or post set in the ground, for guests at a wedding to dance round.
sense: A stake or post set in the ground, for guests at a wedding to dance round.
quote: Divide the broad bridecake Round about the bridestake.
author: B. Jonson

definition: The matter of which the philosopher's stone was believed to be composed.
sense: The matter of which the philosopher's stone was believed to be composed.

definition: Greediness of appetite for flesh.
sense: Greediness of appetite for flesh. [Sportive.] Pope.

definition: A cerecloth used for the special purpose of enveloping a dead body when embalmed.
sense: A cerecloth used for the special purpose of enveloping a dead body when embalmed.
etym: L. cera wax: cf. F. cirement.

definition: Divination by dropping melted wax in water.
sense: Divination by dropping melted wax in water.

definition: Glittering; dressed in, or overlaid with, tinsel finery.
sense: Glittering; dressed in, or overlaid with, tinsel finery. [Obs.]
author: Shak

definition: The sound made when a cork is forcibly drawn from a bottle.
sense: The sound made when a cork is forcibly drawn from a bottle.
quote: "The cloop of a cork wrenched from a bottle."
author: Thackeray

definition: Dying together or at the same time.
sense: Dying together or at the same time. [R.] Sir G. Buck.
etym: L. commoriens, p. pr. of commoriri.

definition: A lamentation for the dead; a dirge.
sense: A lamentation for the dead; a dirge. [Written also coranich, corrinoch, coronach, cronach, etc.] [Scot.]
etym: Gael. coranach, or corranach, a crying, the Irish funeral cry (the keen), a dirge; comh with + ranaich a roaring, ran to roar, shriek.

definition: Divination by means of a suspended sieve.
sense: Divination by means of a suspended sieve.

definition: The act of torturing; torture; torment.
sense: The act of torturing; torture; torment. [Obs.] Bp. Hall.

definition: To grow dark; to show indistinctly.
sense: To grow dark; to show indistinctly. Thackeray.

definition: To make cowardly; to intimidate; to dispirit.
sense: To make cowardly; to intimidate; to dispirit; as, to dastardize my courage. Dryden.

definition: Having a dull, faint heart; spiritless; listless.
sense: Having a dull, faint heart; spiritless; listless.
author: Bp. Hall

definition: To free from a charm; to disenchant.
sense: To free from a charm; to disenchant.

definition: A wandering of the mind; a crazy fancy.
sense: A wandering of the mind; a crazy fancy. [Obs.] Heywood.
etym: L. deliramentum, fr. delirare. See Delirium.

definition: A half wolf; a mongrel dog, between a dog and a wolf.
sense: A half wolf; a mongrel dog, between a dog and a wolf.

definition: To fight like gladiators; to contend fiercely; to dispute violently.
sense: To fight like gladiators; to contend fiercely; to dispute violently. [Obs.]
author: Hales
etym: L. digladiari; di- = dis- + gladius a sword.

definition: To rend asunder; to tear to pieces.
sense: To rend asunder; to tear to pieces. Sir T. Browne.
etym: L. dilaceratus, p. p. of dilacerare to tear apart; di- = dis- + lacerare to tear.

definition: To rend in pieces; to tear.
sense: To rend in pieces; to tear. [R.] Howell.
etym: L. dilaniatus, p. p. of dilaniare to dilacerate; di- = dis- + laniare to tear to pieces.

definition: A tearing apart; violent separation.
sense: A tearing apart; violent separation. [Obs.] Bp. Hall.

definition: The act of killing a master.
sense: The act of killing a master.
etym: L. dominus master + caedere to cut down, kill.

definition: A charming; state of being bewitched or deluded.
sense: A charming; state of being bewitched or deluded. [Obs.]

definition: Sickness; ailment; sorrow.
sense: Sickness; ailment; sorrow. [Obs.] Sir T. Elyot.

definition: A panegyrical funeral oration.
sense: A panegyrical funeral oration.

definition: To make brilliant with beams.
sense: To make brilliant with beams. [R.] G. Fletcher.

definition: A gradual oxidation from exposure to air and moisture, as in the decay of old trees or of dead animals.
sense: A gradual oxidation from exposure to air and moisture, as in the decay of old trees or of dead animals.

definition: The act or operation of burning up.
sense: The act or operation of burning up. Bailey.
etym: L. exustio, fr. exurere, exustum, to burn up; ex out + urere to burn.

definition: Caused or acting by witchcraft.
sense: Caused or acting by witchcraft. [Obs.] "Fascinous diseases." Harvey.
etym: L. fascinum witchcraft, akin to fascinare. See Fascinate.

definition: Fate-bringing; deadly; mortal; destructive.
sense: Fate-bringing; deadly; mortal; destructive. [R.] Johnson.
etym: L. fatifer; fatum fate + ferre to bear, bring.

definition: A frolic; a vagary; a whim.
sense: A frolic; a vagary; a whim. [Obs.] Beau. & Fl.

definition: A nebulous arch, or bow, of white or yellowish light sometimes seen in fog, etc.
sense: A nebulous arch, or bow, of white or yellowish light sometimes seen in fog, etc.

definition: Prognostic; previous omen.
sense: Prognostic; previous omen. Sir P. Sidney.

definition: Food made of hulled wheat boiled in milk, with sugar, plums, etc.
sense: Food made of hulled wheat boiled in milk, with sugar, plums, etc. [Written also furmenty and furmity.] Halliwell.
etym: OF. fromentée, fr. L. frumentum. See Frumentaceous.

definition: Pertaining to soot; sooty; dark; dusky.
sense: Pertaining to soot; sooty; dark; dusky.
etym: L. fuliginosus, from fuligo soot: cf. F. fuligineux. See Fume.

definition: Pertaining to a funeral or funerals; funeral; funereal.
sense: Pertaining to a funeral or funerals; funeral; funereal. [Obs.]
author: Sir T. Browne
etym: L. funebris belonging to a funeral, fr. funus funeral.

definition: A low fellow; a stinkard; a scoundrel.
sense: A low fellow; a stinkard; a scoundrel. [Obs.] Shak.

definition: Full of gashes; hideous; frightful.
sense: Full of gashes; hideous; frightful. [Obs.] "A gashful, horrid, ugly shape." Gayton.

definition: Divination by means of laughter.
sense: Divination by means of laughter.

definition: An ornamental branched candlestick.
sense: An ornamental branched candlestick.

definition: A thick, viscid fluid; a clot, as of blood.
sense: A thick, viscid fluid; a clot, as of blood. Quincy.
etym: OF. grume, cf. F. grumeau a little heap, clot of blood, dim. fr. L. grumus.

definition: Prognostication; soothsaying.
sense: Prognostication; soothsaying. [Obs.] Cockeram.

definition: A cloth for covering a coffin when on a bier; a pall.
sense: A cloth for covering a coffin when on a bier; a pall. Bp.
author: Sanderson

definition: A composition for infernal purposes; a magical preparation.
sense: A composition for infernal purposes; a magical preparation.
author: Shak

definition: A cordial made of spiced wine, etc.
sense: A cordial made of spiced wine, etc.
etym: F. hippocras, hypocras, NL. vinum hippocraticum, lit., wine of Hippocrates.

definition: Sounding dreadfully; uttering a terrible sound.
sense: Sounding dreadfully; uttering a terrible sound. [Obs.] Bailey.
etym: L. horrisonus; horrere to be horrible + sonus a sound.

definition: Above or transcending physical laws; supernatural.
sense: Above or transcending physical laws; supernatural.
quote: Those who do not fly to some hyperphysical hypothesis.
author: Sir W. Hamilton

definition: Appearance or image; a phantasm; a spectral image; also, a mental image or idea.
sense: Appearance or image; a phantasm; a spectral image; also, a mental image or idea.

definition: Produced by the action of fire, as lava.
sense: Produced by the action of fire, as lava. [R.]
etym: L. ignigenus; ignis fire + genere, ginere, to beget, produce.

definition: To cover, as with a mask; to disguise or conceal.
sense: To cover, as with a mask; to disguise or conceal. [R.] Shak.

definition: The act of kindling, or the state of being kindled or on fire.
sense: The act of kindling, or the state of being kindled or on fire.
author: Bacon
etym: L. incensio. See Incense to inflame.

definition: To consume or reduce to ashes by burning, as a dead body; to cremate.
sense: To consume or reduce to ashes by burning, as a dead body; to cremate.

definition: Felt inwardly; heartfelt.
sense: Felt inwardly; heartfelt. [R.]
quote: The baron stood afar off, or knelt in submissive, acknowledged, infelt inferiority.
author: Milman

definition: Having no mirth; not festive or merry; dull; cheerless; gloomy; forlorn.
sense: Having no mirth; not festive or merry; dull; cheerless; gloomy; forlorn. [R.]
etym: L. infestivus. See In- not, and Festive.

definition: Mischievous; harmful; dangerous.
sense: Mischievous; harmful; dangerous. [Obs.] "Infestuous as serpents." Bacon.

definition: The act of chilling or causing to become cold; a chilling; coldness; congelation.
sense: The act of chilling or causing to become cold; a chilling; coldness; congelation. [Obs.] Boyle.

definition: To set a soul in; reflexively, to fix one's strongest affections on.
sense: To set a soul in; reflexively, to fix one's strongest affections on. [Obs.] Jer. Taylor.
quote: [He] could not but insoul himself in her.
author: Feltham

definition: Belonging or pertaining to the time when the moon, at or near its conjunction with the sun, is invisible.
sense: Belonging or pertaining to the time when the moon, at or near its conjunction with the sun, is invisible. Milton.
etym: Pref. inter- + lunar: cf. L. interlunis.

definition: Mutual slaughter or destruction; massacre.
sense: Mutual slaughter or destruction; massacre. [Obs.] Sir M. Hale.

definition: The act of burning or branding.
sense: The act of burning or branding. [Obs.] T. Adams.

definition: The act of shedding tears; weeping.
sense: The act of shedding tears; weeping.
etym: L. lacrimatio, from lacrimare to shed tears, fr. lacrima tear.

definition: A lying in concealment; hiding.
sense: A lying in concealment; hiding. [Obs.]

definition: Flimsy; vague; deceptive.
sense: Flimsy; vague; deceptive. [Obs.] Ascham.
etym: AS. leás void, loose, false. Cf. Leasing.

definition: The use of pretentious words, language, or style.
sense: The use of pretentious words, language, or style.

definition: Crafty; cunning; mischievous; wicked; treacherous; lazy.
sense: Crafty; cunning; mischievous; wicked; treacherous; lazy.[Archaic]
quote: He [the dwarf] was waspish, arch, and litherly.
author: Sir W. Scott

definition: An inhabitant of the moon.
sense: An inhabitant of the moon.

definition: A little moon or satellite.
sense: A little moon or satellite. [Obs.] Bp. Hall.

definition: A killer of men; a manslayer.
sense: A killer of men; a manslayer. [Obs.] Carew.

definition: A flow of sweetness, or a sweet, smooth flow.
sense: A flow of sweetness, or a sweet, smooth flow.

definition: A fermented beverage made of honey and water; mead.
sense: A fermented beverage made of honey and water; mead. Gay.
etym: W. meddyglyn; medd mead + llyn liquor, juice. See Mead a drink.

definition: To happen or come to pass unfortunately; also, to suffer evil fortune.
sense: To happen or come to pass unfortunately; also, to suffer evil fortune. [Obs.]

definition: To ween amiss; to misjudge; to distrust; to be mistaken.
sense: To ween amiss; to misjudge; to distrust; to be mistaken. [Obs.]
author: Spenser

definition: One who fights in single combat; a duelist.
sense: One who fights in single combat; a duelist.

definition: The bright reflection of the moon's light on an expanse of water.
sense: The bright reflection of the moon's light on an expanse of water. [Poetic]

definition: Nothingness; a state of being nothing.
sense: Nothingness; a state of being nothing.

definition: Futility; trifling talk or behavior; drollery.
sense: Futility; trifling talk or behavior; drollery. [R.] Dr. H.
author: More

definition: A portion of food taken at or after noon, usually between full meals; a luncheon.
sense: A portion of food taken at or after noon, usually between full meals; a luncheon. [Written also noonshun.] Hudibras.
etym: OE. nonechenche, for noneschenche, prop., a noon drink; none noon + schenchen, schenken, skinken, to pour, AS. scencan. See Noon, and Skink, v. i.

definition: Done or obtained by surprise; with secrecy, or by concealment of the truth.
sense: Done or obtained by surprise; with secrecy, or by concealment of the truth. [R.] Cotgrave.

definition: Act of darkening or obscuring.
sense: Act of darkening or obscuring. [R.] Sir T. More.

definition: A killing; the act of killing.
sense: A killing; the act of killing. [Obs.] Sir M. Hale.
etym: L.occisio, fr. occidere, occisium, to cut down, to kill; ob (see Ob-) + caedere to cut.

definition: The character or manners of an ogre.
sense: The character or manners of an ogre.

definition: Wandering anywhere and everywhere.
sense: Wandering anywhere and everywhere. [R.]
etym: Omni + L. vagans, p.pr. of vagari to wander.

definition: Eating raw flesh; using uncooked meat as food.
sense: Eating raw flesh; using uncooked meat as food; as, omophagic feasts, rites.

definition: An interpreter of dreams.
sense: An interpreter of dreams. Bp. Warburton. Addison.

definition: Divination by means of dreams.
sense: Divination by means of dreams. De Quincey.

definition: To frown down; to overbear by frowning.
sense: To frown down; to overbear by frowning. Shak.

definition: To quench entirely; to extinguish.
sense: To quench entirely; to extinguish. "The candlelight outquenched." Spenser.

definition: An abode or a haunt of owls.
sense: An abode or a haunt of owls.

definition: A piece of a fallen wall; a ruin.
sense: A piece of a fallen wall; a ruin. [Obs.] Burton.
etym: L. parietinus parietal: cf. parietinae ruined walls.

definition: One who watches or keeps awake all night.
sense: One who watches or keeps awake all night.

definition: Made heavy or dull; debased.
sense: Made heavy or dull; debased. [Obs.] "Pesanted to each lewd thought's control." Marston.

definition: A thick, bushy plot; a thicket.
sense: A thick, bushy plot; a thicket. [Obs.] Chapman.

definition: A specter mentioned to frighten children.
sense: A specter mentioned to frighten children; as, rawhead and bloodybones.

definition: To demolish; to subvert; to destroy; to reduce to poverty; to ruin.
sense: To demolish; to subvert; to destroy; to reduce to poverty; to ruin.
quote: I will not ruinate my fShak. Ruinating thereby the health of their bodies.
author: Burton
etym: LL. ruinatus, p.p. of ruinare to ruin. See Ruin.

definition: Destitute of blood; pale.
sense: Destitute of blood; pale. [R.]

definition: A hired mourner at a funeral.
sense: A hired mourner at a funeral. [Scot.] Sir W. Scott.

definition: Having a red, pimpled face.
sense: Having a red, pimpled face. [Obs.] [Written also sawceflem.]
author: Chaucer
etym: OF. saus salt (L. salsus) + flemme phlegm.

definition: A slight contest; a skirmish.
sense: A slight contest; a skirmish. See Skirmish. [Obs.]
quote: Such cruel game my scarmoges disarms.
author: Spenser

definition: The art or science of projecting or delineating shadows as they fall in nature.
sense: The art or science of projecting or delineating shadows as they fall in nature. Gwilt.

definition: An instrument for writing in the dark, or without seeing.
sense: An instrument for writing in the dark, or without seeing.
author: Maunder

definition: Something that separates; a hedge; a fence.
sense: Something that separates; a hedge; a fence. [R.] Bailey.
etym: L. sepimentum, saepimentum, from sepire, saepire, to hedge in.

definition: Divination by burning straws on red-hot iron, and noting the manner of their burning.
sense: Divination by burning straws on red-hot iron, and noting the manner of their burning. Craig.

definition: To deceive; to cheat; to trick.
sense: To deceive; to cheat; to trick. [Obs.] B. Jonson.

definition: Inclined to sleep; drowsy; sleepy.
sense: Inclined to sleep; drowsy; sleepy. [Obs.]

definition: The murder of one's sister; also, one who murders or kills one's own sister.
sense: The murder of one's sister; also, one who murders or kills one's own sister. Johnson.
etym: L. sororocida, and sororicidium; soror a sister + caedere to kill.

definition: Spirit; mind; soul; state of mind; mood.
sense: Spirit; mind; soul; state of mind; mood. [Obs.] "The high heroic spright." Spenser.
quote: Wondrous great grief groweth in my spright.
author: Spenser

definition: To die, or cause to die; to perish.
sense: To die, or cause to die; to perish. See Starve. [Obs.] Chaucer.
author: Spenser

definition: Stout; sullen; obstinate.
sense: Stout; sullen; obstinate. [Obs.]
quote: With stern looks and stomachous disdain.
author: Spenser
etym: L. stomachosus angry, peexish. See Stomach.

definition: A direct descending blow with the edge of a sword.
sense: A direct descending blow with the edge of a sword. [Obs.] B.
author: Jonson

definition: Situated beneath the moon; hence, of or pertaining to this world; terrestrial; earthly.
sense: Situated beneath the moon; hence, of or pertaining to this world; terrestrial; earthly.
quote: All things sublunary are subject to change. Dryden. All sublunary comforts imitate the changeableness, as well as feel the influence, of the planet they are under.
author: South
etym: Pref. sub + lunar, or lunary: cf. F. sublunaire.

definition: A kind of amulet or magical charm.
sense: A kind of amulet or magical charm. [Obs.] J. Gregory.

definition: Deathlike; resembling death.
sense: Deathlike; resembling death. Dunglison.

definition: The act of fuming with incense, or the act of burning incense.
sense: The act of fuming with incense, or the act of burning incense.
etym: L. thus incense + -ficare (in comp.) to make. See -fy.

definition: A noise like that made by a clock or a watch.
sense: A noise like that made by a clock or a watch.
etym: See Tick to beat, to pat, and (for sense 2) cf. Tricktrack.

definition: An ornamental firework which turns round, when in the air, so as to form a scroll of fire.
sense: An ornamental firework which turns round, when in the air, so as to form a scroll of fire. G. Francis.
etym: F. torbillion a whirlwind, tourbillion, fr. L. turbo, -inis, a whirl, whirlwind.

definition: Work or devices suitable to be concealed; a secret stratagem.
sense: Work or devices suitable to be concealed; a secret stratagem. [Obs.]

definition: To shade; to shadow; to foreshadow.
sense: To shade; to shadow; to foreshadow. [Obs.]
etym: L. umbratus, p. p. of umbrare to shade, fr. umbra a shade.

definition: To unwind, unfold, or untie; hence, to undo; to ruin.
sense: To unwind, unfold, or untie; hence, to undo; to ruin. Shak.

definition: To deprive of existence; to annihilate.
sense: To deprive of existence; to annihilate.
quote: Who can uncreate thee, thou shalt know.
author: Milton

definition: To free from a curse or an execration.
sense: To free from a curse or an execration. Shak.

definition: To creep secretly or privily.
sense: To creep secretly or privily. [Obs.] Wyclif.

definition: The burden of a song; the chorus; the refrain.
sense: The burden of a song; the chorus; the refrain. Dryden.

definition: To raise or remove from the grave; to disinter; to untomb; to exhume.
sense: To raise or remove from the grave; to disinter; to untomb; to exhume. [Obs.] Fuller.

definition: To open, as the eyes of a hawk that have been seeled; hence, to give light to; to enlighten.
sense: To open, as the eyes of a hawk that have been seeled; hence, to give light to; to enlighten. [Obs.] B. Jonson.

definition: To deprive of soul, spirit, or principle.
sense: To deprive of soul, spirit, or principle. [R.] Shelton.

definition: Having the quality of burning.
sense: Having the quality of burning. [R.] I. Watts.

definition: Containing, or full of, worms; resembling worms.
sense: Containing, or full of, worms; resembling worms.

definition: The act of putting to death every twentieth man.
sense: The act of putting to death every twentieth man. [R.]

definition: Preparation; protection; provision; supply.
sense: Preparation; protection; provision; supply. [Obs.]
etym: OF. warison safety, supplies, cure, F. guérison cure. See Warish, v. t.

definition: Full of wiles; trickish; deceitful.
sense: Full of wiles; trickish; deceitful.
